credits.title: Credits
credits.heading: Credits & Info
credits.about.what_body: FlexDex is a fan-made toolkit for Pokémon GO players: raid counters, DPS calculations, PvP IV rankings, a full shiny Pokémon dex, a personal shiny collection tracker, a Trainer Directory, and a live Raid Finder for coordinating remote raids with other players.
credits.about.disclaimer: The site is not affiliated with Niantic, The Pokémon Company, or Nintendo.
credits.about.source_pogoapi: Pokémon stats, moves, type effectiveness, shiny availability, CP multipliers
credits.about.source_pokeminers: mined costume art for the shiny dex, served from our own cache
credits.about.source_masterfile: costume and form names behind the costume picker
credits.about.source_dittobase: cross-checking costume names and release events
credits.about.source_pokeapi: Pokémon sprites, Pokédex flavor text, genus, legendary/mythical flags, in-game cries, and official localized Pokémon names
credits.about.source_openmeteo: current weather data used to determine Pokémon GO weather boosts
credits.about.source_scrapedduck: current and upcoming event data, full event details, and event images, from LeekDuck
credits.about.source_showdown: trainer class and named character sprites for the Classic avatar set
credits.about.source_dreamstone: GBA-style trainer sprites for the Dreamstone avatar set
credits.about.source_pex: FRLG-style trainer sprites for the pokeemerald-expansion avatar set
credits.about.source_platinum: native Gen 4 Diamond/Pearl/Platinum trainer sprites for the Platinum avatar set
credits.api.public_body: The following endpoints are publicly accessible and return game data as JSON. Two limits apply per IP: a per-endpoint request rate limit and an aggregate bandwidth cap across all endpoints in this table combined.
credits.api.data_desc: All game data in one payload (Pokémon, moves, raids, shinies, type chart, CP multipliers)
credits.api.maxbattles_desc: Current Max Battle bosses by tier
credits.api.events_desc: Current and upcoming events (LeekDuck via ScrapedDuck)
credits.api.event_detail_desc: Full details for one event (sanitized HTML from LeekDuck)
credits.api.bw_note: Bandwidth limit: 25 MB total across all endpoints per 5-minute window, counted as the compressed bytes actually sent (ask for gzip and it goes much further). Exceeding it triggers a 10-minute block.
credits.api.cache_note2: Game data refreshes every 6 hours; events every 30 minutes; raid bosses every 4 hours on Mountain Time.
credits.api.community_body: These endpoints return per-user profile data. No rate limit applies, but profile-scoped endpoints respect privacy settings and return an empty result rather than an error when data is not visible.
credits.api.awards_desc: Full awards catalog with names, descriptions, and icons
credits.api.awards_of_desc: Awards earned by a specific user
credits.api.shinies_of_desc: A user's public shiny collection; empty array if their profile is private or they have hidden their collection in Settings
credits.api.private_body: The private API is intended for trusted server-side consumers. It exposes the same data as the public API with no rate limiting, but requires an account with API access granted by the site superadmin.
credits.api.private_maxbattles_desc: Current Max Battle bosses (same as public)
credits.api.private_refresh_desc: Force an immediate refresh of all cached game data (rate-limited to 2 per 10 minutes globally)
credits.api.private_auth: Authentication uses your session cookie. Contact the site operator if you need access.
credits.api.your_access_body: Your account has been granted access to the private API. The private endpoints mirror the public API but carry no rate limit and are intended for trusted server-side use.
credits.api.your_access_cookie_note: Include the hgo_session cookie in each request. Find its value in your browser's developer tools: Application → Cookies → pogo.hails.app.
credits.api.your_access_warning: Keep your session token private. If you believe it has been exposed, log out and back in to generate a new one.
credits.api.note_rate_limit: Exceeding the public rate limit returns
credits.api.note_unofficial: This is an unofficial fan-made toolkit. New fields can appear in responses at any time, so read only the ones you use and ignore the rest. Anything being removed is deprecated and announced ahead of time.
credits.changelog.intro: A running log of updates and improvements.

credits.about.playtest_body: FlexDex for Android is in open beta. Anyone with an Android phone can join and help test it.
playtest.title: Playtest
playtest.heading: Playtest FlexDex for Android
playtest.lede: Help test the FlexDex Android app before it reaches Google Play. This guide takes you through everything, one small step at a time, with a picture of every screen you will see. Tick each step off as you go; this page remembers where you are, so you can leave and come back.
playtest.start.title: Two quick questions
playtest.start.q_account: Do you already have a FlexDex account on this website?
playtest.start.signed_in: You are signed in, so your account is ready. The guide starts at joining the beta.
playtest.start.q_device: Which device are you on right now?
playtest.start.android: You are on an Android phone. Follow the guide right here on this phone.
playtest.start.iphone: There is no iPhone version of FlexDex. The playtest is for Android phones only.
playtest.start.desktop: You are on a computer. The install steps happen on your Android phone, so open this page there. You can still make your FlexDex account here first.
playtest.start.copy: Copy the link to this page
playtest.start.all: Show every step on one page
playtest.start.guided: Back to one step at a time
playtest.account.title: You need a FlexDex account to sign in to the app
playtest.account.body: Anyone can join the beta, but the app itself only works once you sign in with a FlexDex account: the same username and password you use on this website. It is free, and Step 1 shows you how to make one.
playtest.ui.zoom: Tap the picture to see it bigger
playtest.st.account.title: Create your FlexDex account
playtest.st.account.intro: This is your account for this website and for the app. Skip this step if you already have one.
playtest.st.join.title: Join the beta
playtest.st.join.intro: Sign up as a tester with Firebase, Google's service for sharing test versions of apps. Do this on your Android phone.
playtest.st.tester.title: Install Firebase App Tester
playtest.st.tester.intro: App Tester is Google's app for installing test versions. FlexDex is installed from inside it, and it is how you get every update.
playtest.st.signin.title: Sign in to App Tester
playtest.st.signin.intro: App Tester needs to know which tester you are. This is where the Google account has to match.
playtest.st.install.title: Install FlexDex
playtest.st.install.intro: Now the app itself. It is about 50 MB, so Wi-Fi is a good idea.
playtest.st.first.title: First launch
playtest.st.first.intro: Open FlexDex for the first time and sign in.
playtest.c.acc_register.title: Open Create account and fill in three fields
playtest.c.acc_register.body: Username: 2 to 32 characters, letters, numbers, _ and - only. It is your login and the name other trainers see. Email: used to confirm your account and to reset your password. Password: at least 8 characters. Then tap Create Account.
playtest.c.acc_confirm.title: Confirm your email
playtest.c.acc_confirm.body: A confirmation email is on its way. Open it and tap the link. Until you do, a banner at the top of the site reminds you; tap Resend email if it did not arrive (check your spam folder too). Nothing is locked while you wait.
playtest.c.acc_profile.title: Fill in your trainer basics
playtest.c.acc_profile.body: Open Settings, Trainer Profile. Add your in-game Trainer Name and your Trainer Code (your 12-digit friend code; spaces are fine). Add your Trainer Level too: the app uses it to make IV scans more accurate. Tap Save. All of this is optional, but the app works best with it.
playtest.c.acc_location.title: Add your city for weather boosts (optional)
playtest.c.acc_location.body: Under Location and Privacy, your City is used only to work out which Pokémon are weather boosted near you. It is never shown publicly. Location Visibility controls what, if anything, the Trainer Directory shows.
playtest.c.acc_two.title: Two different accounts
playtest.c.acc_two.body: Your FlexDex account (the username and password you just made) is for this website and the app. Your Google account is only for joining the beta through Firebase. They do not need to match each other.
playtest.c.acc_signin.title: One login for the site and the app
playtest.c.acc_signin.body: You will sign in to the app with this same username and password. The app's sign in screen also has Create an account and Forgot your password?, so you can do either of those from your phone too.
playtest.c.join_open.title: Open the invite and sign in with Google
playtest.c.join_open.body: Tap Join the open beta below on your phone. If Google asks you to sign in, choose the Google account that is already on your phone. If your phone is signed in, you may skip straight to the next screen.
playtest.c.join_signup.title: Check the email, then tap Sign up
playtest.c.join_signup.body: "Ready to test this app?" shows FlexDex with your Google email already filled in. Make sure it is the Google account on your phone, the one App Tester will use later. If they are different, FlexDex will not show up for you. Then tap Sign up.
playtest.c.join_in.title: You're in!
playtest.c.join_in.body: Firebase also sends you an invitation email (from Firebase App Distribution, about testing FlexDex). You do not need to wait for it: carry on with the next screen. If you lose your place, the link in that email brings you back here.
playtest.c.join_accept.title: Tap Accept invitation
playtest.c.join_accept.body: The Test apps page lists FlexDex (Pending). Tap Accept invitation under it.
playtest.c.join_consent.title: Tick the box, then Accept invitation
playtest.c.join_consent.body: "Accept invitation as:" shows the Google account you are using; tap Switch if it is the wrong one. Tick the consent box (the button stays gray until you do), then tap Accept invitation.
playtest.c.join_release.title: Skip this Download button
playtest.c.join_release.body: You now see FlexDex with a Download button. Do not use it: install App Tester instead (next step), because App Tester is what keeps FlexDex up to date. Look for the bar at the bottom: "Get the Firebase App Tester app" with Download App Tester.
playtest.c.t_intro.title: Why Android will ask twice about unknown apps
playtest.c.t_intro.body: App Tester is not on Google Play; Google only offers it as a download from this page. Android protects you from apps that come from outside Google Play by asking first, so you will see an "unknown apps" question twice: once for your browser (now) and once for App Tester (when it installs FlexDex). Both are expected. App Tester is Google's own app, and you can switch the setting off again afterwards.
playtest.c.t_download.title: Tap Download App Tester, then Download
playtest.c.t_download.body: Chrome asks "Choose where to download" for app-tester.apk (about 5 MB). Leave the folder as it is and tap Download.
playtest.c.t_harmful.title: Tap Download anyway
playtest.c.t_harmful.body: Chrome warns "File might be harmful". It says this about every app downloaded outside Google Play, not because of anything in App Tester. Tap Download anyway.
playtest.c.t_open.title: Tap Open
playtest.c.t_open.body: When "File downloaded" appears, tap Open. Missed it? Open your phone's Downloads (or Files) app and tap app-tester.apk.
playtest.c.t_blocked.title: Tap Settings
playtest.c.t_blocked.body: Android says your phone "currently isn't allowed to install unknown apps from this source". That is the first unknown apps question. Tap Settings.
playtest.c.t_allow.title: Turn on Allow from this source, then go back
playtest.c.t_allow.body: Switch on Allow from this source, then tap the back arrow. This lets your browser install App Tester. You can switch it off again once you are done.
playtest.c.t_install.title: Tap Install
playtest.c.t_install.body: "App Tester: Do you want to install this app?" Tap Install.
playtest.c.t_done.title: Tap Open
playtest.c.t_done.body: "App installed." Tap Open to start App Tester.
playtest.c.s_google.title: Tap Sign in with Google
playtest.c.s_google.body: App Tester opens on its welcome screen. Tap Sign in with Google.
playtest.c.s_choose.title: Choose the same Google account you signed up with
playtest.c.s_choose.body: This is where most people go wrong. Pick exactly the account you used in Step 2. A different account signs in fine, but FlexDex will not appear in it.
playtest.c.s_share.title: Tap Continue
playtest.c.s_share.body: "Sign in to Firebase App Distribution" explains that your name and email are shared with App Tester. Tap Continue.
playtest.c.s_access.title: Tick the box first, then Continue
playtest.c.s_access.body: "Firebase App Distribution wants access to your Google Account." The checkbox next to "See, edit, create and delete your Firebase App Distribution tester data" starts unticked. Tick it, scroll down, then tap Continue. This is the easiest step to miss.
playtest.c.s_list.title: Tap FlexDex
playtest.c.s_list.body: Test apps now lists FlexDex. Tap it.
playtest.c.s_start.title: Tick the box, then START TESTING ON THIS DEVICE
playtest.c.s_start.body: Tick the consent box, then tap START TESTING ON THIS DEVICE.
playtest.c.i_download.title: Tap Download
playtest.c.i_download.body: The FlexDex page says "No release installed". The newest release is at the top of the list, with its notes underneath. Tap Download.
playtest.c.i_notif.title: Allow App Tester's notifications
playtest.c.i_notif.body: App Tester asks to send you notifications. Tap Allow: that is how you hear about new builds.
playtest.c.i_wait.title: Wait for the download
playtest.c.i_wait.body: FlexDex is about 50 MB. The bar shows how far along it is.
playtest.c.i_unknown.title: The second unknown apps question: allow it for App Tester
playtest.c.i_unknown.body: Android asks again, this time about App Tester. Tap Settings, switch on Allow from this source, then tap the back arrow. Same as before, and just as expected.
playtest.c.i_install.title: Tap Install
playtest.c.i_install.body: The button now says Install. Tap it, and when Android asks "FlexDex: Do you want to install this app?", tap Install again.
playtest.c.i_open.title: Tap Open
playtest.c.i_open.body: App Tester shows the version you installed. Tap Open. From now on FlexDex is also with your other apps.
playtest.c.f_notif.title: Allow FlexDex's notifications
playtest.c.f_notif.body: FlexDex asks to send you notifications, for raid lobbies and event reminders. Tap Allow if you want them; you can change this later in your phone's settings.
playtest.c.f_login.title: Sign in with your FlexDex account
playtest.c.f_login.body: "Welcome back." Enter your FlexDex username and password from Step 1, not your Google account. If your password manager saved them for the website, it can fill them in.
playtest.c.f_perms.title: Two more permissions, later
playtest.c.f_perms.body: When you first start the IV scanner, Android asks for two more things. Display over other apps lets the scanner's small floating bubble sit on top of Pokémon GO. Screen capture ("start recording or casting") lets the scanner read the appraisal from your screen; Android asks every time a scanning session starts. The screen image is read on your phone and is never uploaded or saved.
playtest.done.title: You're all set!
playtest.done.body: FlexDex is installed and signed in. Thank you for testing! Below is how updates reach you, help for common problems, and how to report anything that goes wrong.
playtest.updates.title: How updates reach you
playtest.updates.intro: New test versions come out regularly. You will know about each one in three ways:
playtest.updates.email: Firebase emails you that a new build of FlexDex is ready to test.
playtest.updates.tester: App Tester lists the new build (and notifies you, if you allowed it). Open it and tap to download and install. It installs over the old version and keeps your data.
playtest.updates.card: Inside FlexDex, a "New build" card appears at the top of Home the next time you open the app. It says which build is available and which one you have, with an Update button that takes you to App Tester. You can close the card; it comes back when the next build is out. The More menu also shows when an update is waiting.
playtest.updates.build: Builds are numbered. To see which one you have, open App settings in FlexDex and look under "This build".
playtest.updates.rollback: If a new build gives you trouble, App Tester lets you install an earlier one.
playtest.help.title: Help and common problems
playtest.help.q_missing: I installed App Tester, but FlexDex is not there.
playtest.help.a_missing: App Tester is signed in with a different Google account than the one you signed up with. Sign out of App Tester and sign back in with the address you signed up with. Or go back to Step 2 and sign up again using the Google account your phone uses.
playtest.help.q_email: The invitation or update email never arrived.
playtest.help.a_email: Check your spam and promotions folders. The email goes to the address you signed up with, so make sure that is the one you are checking. You do not need the invitation email to carry on: the guide's next screens work without it.
playtest.help.q_notinstalled: Android says "App not installed", or asks to uninstall FlexDex.
playtest.help.a_notinstalled: An older copy of FlexDex from somewhere else is already on your phone, and Android will not install over it. Uninstall the old copy first (Android may offer this itself). Its data on the phone goes with it, but your account and everything saved on the website are safe. Then install again from App Tester.
playtest.help.q_signin: App Tester keeps asking me to sign in.
playtest.help.a_signin: Sign in with the same Google account you signed up with, and remember to tick the access checkbox before tapping Continue. If it keeps asking, close App Tester completely and open it again.
playtest.help.q_bubble: The scanner bubble does not appear.
playtest.help.a_bubble: "Display over other apps" is probably off. Open your phone's Settings, find FlexDex under Apps, and turn on "Display over other apps". Then start the scanner again.
playtest.help.q_login: The app will not accept my username or password.
playtest.help.a_login: The app uses your FlexDex website account, not your Google account. Check that you can sign in on this website with the same details. If you forgot your password, reset it on this website.
playtest.help.q_leave: How do I leave the beta?
playtest.help.a_leave: Uninstall FlexDex like any other app. To remove your beta account completely, sign in at the Firebase tester page and open your account overview: the trash icon next to FlexDex leaves just this app, and Delete account removes your tester account entirely. Removing Google's permissions alone does not delete it.
playtest.report.title: Reporting problems
playtest.report.p1: If the app crashes, the crash is reported automatically. You do not need to do anything.
playtest.report.p2: For anything else (something looks wrong, a feature does not work, an idea), use Reports in the app's More menu, or the report button on this website. The more detail you give, the faster it gets fixed.
playtest.privacy.title: Privacy
playtest.privacy.p1: To run the beta, Firebase (a Google service) receives the email address you sign up with. It uses it to send you invitations and update emails and to let you install test versions.
playtest.privacy.p2: How FlexDex itself handles your data is explained on the Privacy page.
playtest.banner.title: Try FlexDex for Android
playtest.banner.sub: Join the open beta and help test the app before it reaches Google Play.
playtest.safe.title: Is FlexDex safe to install?
playtest.safe.p1: Every release of FlexDex is scanned on VirusTotal, a free service that checks a file with dozens of antivirus engines from different security companies. The report is public, so you can look for yourself.
playtest.safe.clean: no security vendor flagged this build.
playtest.safe.hash: SHA-256 fingerprint of this build (it matches the file App Tester installs):
playtest.safe.p2: A clean scan is good evidence, not a guarantee. App Tester itself is Google's own app, and Chrome's "File might be harmful" warning appears for every app downloaded outside Google Play.
playtest.report.p3: Can't get as far as the app? Email
playtest.faq_link: Questions first? Read the FAQ: is it safe, how updates work, and help
playtest.safe.who: FlexDex is a hobby project, made and run by one person, for fun. It is not a company, and there is no catch.
playtest.safe.choice: If installing an app from outside Google Play does not feel right to you, that is completely okay. Nobody is being pushed to join the beta. FlexDex will come to the Google Play Store in time, and you can simply wait for it there; the website works the same either way.
store.cosmetic_only: Supporters only ever get cosmetics, like a supporter badge and a rainbow name. Never anything that gives an advantage.
